target.title: fix(scripts): preserve emoji in realtime smoke diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Google Live realtime-talk smoke diagnostics when an incoming WebSocket frame reaches the 300-code-unit preview boundary at an emoji. It also keeps the final frame visible when an abnormal close follows immediately after a message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Live event payloads are external text and can contain arbitrary Unicode. The original page-side `slice(0, 300)` could cut a surrogate pair before the debug snapshot was serialized. An initial host callback avoided that cut but introduced an asynchronous gap between the message and close handlers.

The final implementation sets browser frames to `arraybuffer`, captures a bounded structured snapshot synchronously before parsing, and returns failures as data. It retains at most eight complete messages up to 16 Ki UTF-16 code units each; oversized frames are replaced wholesale with a content-free length marker, so structured secrets are never cut before redaction. Node then applies the existing dev-tool redactor and UTF-16-safe preview to complete retained messages and close reasons before constructing the diagnostic.

## User Impact

Realtime-talk smoke failures now preserve message ordering and report bounded, redacted, valid-Unicode diagnostics at emoji boundaries.

## Evidence

- Exact head `5a302aee5b1`, rebased once onto latest submission-time `main` `e3618454f24`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/dev-tooling-safety.test.ts` on Node 24.15.0: 64 tests passed after the rebase.
- Final abnormal-close diagnostic regression covers a 296-code-unit prefix followed by an emoji and verifies no emoji tail leaks.
- Structured-secret regression verifies redaction runs before the 300-code-unit preview.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh pre-submit autoreview reported no actionable findings.
- A live Google API run was not performed because no Google/Gemini API key is available in this environment; the actual browser transport remains covered by repository CI while the final diagnostic construction and boundary behavior are covered by focused tests.
